fact_rationales.F10: The milky white layer on the blood sample is characteristic of lipoprotein lipase deficiency, which leads to an accumulation of chylomicrons in the blood, giving it a milky appearance.

Milky white layer on blood sample surface is characteristic of lipoprotein disorders, which includes Familial chylomicronemia syndrome and is also seen in Glycogen storage disease type 1 due to associated hypertriglyceridemia.
fact_rationales.F3: Decline in length percentile can be seen in various metabolic disorders due to malnutrition or metabolic derangements, making it less specific but still supportive of a diagnosis like Glycogen storage disease type 1 or Familial chylomicronemia syndrome.
fact_rationales.F6: Significantly distended abdomen can be seen in Glycogen storage disease type 1 due to hepatomegaly and in Familial chylomicronemia syndrome due to the accumulation of chylomicrons.
fact_rationales.F8: Hepatomegaly, indicated by liver edge extending to iliac crest, is a common feature of Glycogen storage disease type 1 and can also occur in other metabolic disorders.
